message.content:
**Proteins that are commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Functions | Representative Examples | |----------|-------------------|-------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; act as channels, transporters, receptors, or anchors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Ionotropic glutamate receptors** (e.g., NMDA receptor)
• **Voltage‑gated ion channels** – e.g., Nav1.5 (sodium), Kv1.2 (potassium)
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels)
• **Integrins** (cell‑matrix adhesion)
• **Cadherins** (cell‑cell adhesion) | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface (inner or outer leaflet) via electrostatic or lipid‑anchor interactions. | • **Actin** (inner leaflet, cytoskeleton)
• **Spectrin** (inner leaflet, cytoskeleton)
• **Ankyrin** (links integral proteins to cytoskeleton)
• **Clathrin** (vesicle coat, inner leaflet)
• **Caveolin** (inner leaflet, caveolae formation)
• **Flotillin** (lipid‑raft marker, inner leaflet)
• **Glycophorin A** (outer leaflet, erythrocyte membrane) | | **Glycoproteins / glycolipids** | Often serve as cell‑surface markers or mediators of cell‑cell recognition. | • **CD molecules** (e.g., CD4, CD8, CD45)
• **MHC class I & II** (antigen presentation)
• **Selectins** (cell adhesion)
• **Heparan sulfate proteoglycans** (growth factor binding) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids (e.g., GPI anchors) and reside on the outer leaflet. | • **CD59** (protectin)
• **Prion protein (PrP^C)** (GPI‑anchored)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** (e.g., EGFR) can be GPI‑anchored in some contexts | ### How to think about plasma‑membrane proteins 1. **Transmembrane vs. peripheral** – Transmembrane proteins cross the bilayer; peripheral proteins sit on one side. 2. **Functional classes** – Channels, transporters, pumps, receptors, adhesion molecules, enzymes, cytoskeletal anchors. 3. **Post‑translational modifications** – Many membrane proteins are glycosylated, phosphorylated, or lipid‑anchored, which influences their localization and function. If you need a more exhaustive list for a particular cell type or organism, let me know!
